payload.prompt: Einer Ihrer Kunden hat eine uberfallige Rechnung. Finden Sie die uberfallige Rechnung und buchen Sie eine Mahngebuhr von 70 NOK. Soll Forderungen (1500), Haben Mahngebuhren (3400). Erstellen Sie außerdem eine Rechnung über die Mahngebühr an den Kunden und senden Sie diese. Registrieren Sie zusätzlich eine Teilzahlung von 5000 NOK auf der überfälligen Rechnung.

payload.goal: Find an overdue customer invoice, add a 70 NOK dunning fee via ledger posting (debit receivables 1500, credit dunning fees 3400), create and send an invoice for the dunning fee to the same customer, and register a partial payment of 5000 NOK on the overdue invoice.
likely_resources: invoice list/search endpoint with overdue status
success_checks: An overdue customer invoice is identified.
A voucher is posted with debit account 1500 = 70 NOK and credit account 3400 = 70 NOK, linked/referenced to the overdue case if possible.
A 70 NOK invoice for the dunning fee is created for the same customer.
The dunning fee invoice is sent to the customer.
A payment of 5000 NOK is registered against the overdue invoice and the remaining balance is reduced accordingly.
risk_notes: Sandbox is empty, so no actual overdue invoice/customer may exist; may need bootstrap data or fail to find target invoice.
Prompt does not specify which customer/invoice; selection criteria for 'the overdue invoice' are ambiguous if multiple exist.
No VAT treatment stated for the dunning fee invoice; fee may be outside VAT scope in some contexts, but prompt does not say. VAT should likely be 0 or omitted depending on system rules.
Sending invoice requires customer contact method (email/e-invoice) not provided.
Payment date, invoice date, due date, and bank account details are not provided and may be required.
Direct posting to 1500/3400 may require open accounting period and valid voucher series.
payload.suggested_first_action: List/search customer invoices filtered to overdue status and select the target overdue invoice.
ordered_steps: GET overdue invoices via invoice list/search endpoint filtered by due date/status.
If no overdue invoice exists in empty sandbox: create bootstrap customer, product/service, order, invoice, and set due date in past so invoice becomes overdue.
Ensure company/bank account settings exist for invoicing and payment registration.
Identify the customer tied to the overdue invoice and capture invoice/customer IDs.
POST voucher on accounting voucher endpoint: debit 1500 receivables 70 NOK, credit 3400 dunning fees 70 NOK; include description/reference to overdue invoice.
If a fee product does not exist, create product 'Mahngebühr' priced 70 NOK with appropriate VAT handling per accounting policy.
Create order for the same customer with one line: Mahngebühr x1 at 70 NOK.
Create invoice from the order for 70 NOK.
Send the dunning fee invoice using invoice send endpoint; if no email/e-delivery target exists, update customer contact or note send-blocker.
Register payment of 5000 NOK on the overdue invoice via payment endpoint, using a valid payment date and bank/cash account.
Verify overdue invoice balance decreased by 5000 NOK and payment is posted.
Verify dunning fee invoice exists and has sent status or queued delivery status.

planned_endpoints.summary: Find accounts corresponding with sent data.
Create customer. Related customer addresses may also be created.
Find products corresponding with sent data.
Create order line. When creating several order lines, use /list for better performance.
Create invoice. Related Order and OrderLines can be created first, or included as new objects inside the Invoice.
Find payment type corresponding with sent data.
Update invoice. The invoice is updated with payment information. The amount is in the invoice’s currency.
Find vouchers corresponding with sent data.
Reverses the voucher, and returns the reversed voucher. Supports reversing most voucher types, except salary transactions.

rules: Use ?number=XXXX to resolve a specific account number to its ID.
Do NOT use other query params — they are not supported.
Do NOT use /ledger/accountingPeriod — it does not exist.
For bank account setup: isBankAccount=true, bankAccountNumber='12345678903', bankAccountCountry={"id": 161}.
MUST include id and version from the GET response.
When email is provided, ALWAYS set BOTH email AND invoiceEmail to the same value.
Do NOT send isCustomer (it's readOnly and auto-set).
For addresses, use postalAddress={addressLine1, postalCode, city, country={id: 161}} for Norway.
ALWAYS search first if product_number is provided: GET /product?number=<number> — sandbox pre-seeds products.
Only POST /product if GET returns 0 results.
Use 'number' field for the product number (NOT productNumber).
priceExcludingVat sets the base price. Also set vatType={"id": 3|5|6}.
Requires customer={"id": customer_id}.
Set orderDate and deliveryDate (use today_iso from execution_brief).
When a product was created, ALWAYS include product={"id": product_id} on the orderline.
Use unitPriceExcludingVatCurrency for the price field.
Set vatType={"id": 3} for 25%, {"id": 5} for 15%, {"id": 6} for 0%.
For multiple lines, prefer POST /order/orderline/list for efficiency.
Pass orders=[{"id": order_id}] to link order.
Set invoiceDate and invoiceDueDate.
Bank account 1920 MUST be configured first (see bank account setup pattern).
Method is PUT, not POST.
ALL params are QUERY PARAMETERS — NOT in body: PUT /invoice/{id}/:payment?paymentDate=YYYY-MM-DD&paymentTypeId=XXXXX&paidAmount=YYYYY
Do NOT send a JSON body — send empty body or no body. ALL data goes in the URL query string.
Get paymentTypeId first via GET /invoice/paymentType — use the first result's id.
paidAmount is the full payment amount (e.g., 47200). For foreign currency, use paidAmountCurrency instead.
Method is PUT, not POST.
date is a QUERY PARAMETER: PUT /ledger/voucher/{id}/:reverse?date=YYYY-MM-DD
Do NOT send date in the request body.
